title: Geonormal dim one smooth
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $Z$ a finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $\dim Z\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Suppose $Z$ is geometrically normal: every local ring of $Z_L=Z\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-fibre-product] for every field extension $L/k$. Then $Z$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and geometrically reduced over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Moreover, for any field extension $L/k$, if $Z_L$ is connected and nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme], then $Z_L$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components].

proof.text: Fix any field extension $L/k$. Choose a finite affine cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $Z$ with each $A_i$ finitely generated over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with $R=k$, $A=A_i$ and $B=L$ to each $U_i$: its scalar extension is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_k L)$. These are the inverse-image open subsets of $Z_L$ and cover it. Indeed, for the open subscheme $U_i\subseteq Z$, a map $T\to Z$ factors through $U_i$ precisely when its image is contained in $U_i$; the pullback universal property therefore identifies the pullback with the open subscheme on the inverse image. If $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ generate $A_i$, then $a_1\otimes1,\ldots,a_r\otimes1$ generate $A_i\otimes_kL$ over $L$ by expanding pure tensors. Thus $Z_L$ is finite type over $L$. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the whole ring, so $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is Noetherian. [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] now shows that $Z_L$ is Noetherian; in particular all its local rings are Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0GK5 proof, normal implies regular in dimension at most one; affine scalar extension by Schemes Tag 01JQ; Noetherianity by Morphisms Tag 01T6

proof.text: Every $U_i$ has dimension at most one: a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $U_i$ gives such a chain in $Z$ by taking closures, since intersecting the closures back with $U_i$ recovers the original subsets. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension], $\dim\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_k A_i)=\dim U_i\le1$; tensor symmetry identifies this spectrum with the chart in step 1. For $x\in Z_L$ choose such a chart containing $x$. Its stalk is $\mathcal O_{Z_L,x}$ because restriction to an open neighbourhood does not change the germs. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], its dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets beginning with $\overline{\{x\}}$ in that chart. These are among the chains measuring the dimension of the chart, so $\dim\mathcal O_{Z_L,x}\le1$. This argument works for arbitrary $L/k$, not just algebraic extensions.

source.place: Tag 00P3 (lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension); Properties Tag 02IZ for local dimensions

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{Z_L,x}$. Geometric normality supplies an integrally closed domain $R$, and step 1 supplies Noetherianity. Since $R$ is a nonzero local domain, its dimension is either zero or one by step 2. If its dimension is zero, the prime ideal $(0)$ cannot be strictly contained in its maximal ideal, so that maximal ideal is zero. Every nonzero element is therefore a unit: $R$ is a field, and its zero maximal ideal is generated by the empty family, making it regular of dimension zero. If its dimension is one, [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes $R$ a discrete valuation ring. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] its maximal ideal is principal; a single generator and $\dim R=1$ give precisely the definition of a regular local ring. Thus every local ring of every $Z_L$ is regular. Together with the Noetherianity from step 1, this says that $Z_L$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 0BX2 (lemma-normal-dimension-1-regular); Algebra Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), (5) implies (1), and the definition of regular local ring

proof.text: In particular the regularity in step 3 holds for every finitely generated field extension $L/k$. The structure morphism of $Z$ is locally of finite type by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-smooth-field-criterion] to obtain smoothness over $k$. This uses geometric regularity, rather than regularity over $k$ alone; no perfectness assumption on $k$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), as used in the proof of Tag 0GK5

proof.text: For every $L/k$, every local ring of $Z_L$ is a domain by the hypothesis of geometric normality. A nilpotent element $a$ of a domain is zero: from $a^n=0$, induction and the absence of zero divisors give $a=0$. Thus all these stalks are reduced, and [def-pc-reduced-scheme] says exactly that $Z_L$ is reduced. Quantifying over $L$ is geometric reducedness as defined in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Geometric reducedness, Definition Tag 035V; geometric normality in the proof of Tag 0GK5

proof.text: Finally let $L/k$ be such that $Z_L$ is connected and nonempty. Step 3 makes $Z_L$ regular, so [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] applies and makes it integral. [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible] gives irreducibility of its underlying space. For the empty scheme the smoothness and reducedness assertions above are vacuous locally, while the final implication has a false antecedent; disconnected regular base changes are not asserted to be irreducible.
